answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in a bond before it may vote or claim rewards. The protocol can slash that bond when independent audits show coordinated duplicate accounts, while honest agents recover it after a waiting period. This makes a Sybil attack costly: an attacker must buy and immobilize many tokens, risking forfeiture, rather than merely minting names. The river of identities may look broad, but saffron-colored profiles and meadow-like activity do not substitute for capital at risk.
